extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense public affairs officers, PA/VI personnel, commanders, and PA planners involved in domestic operations (DSCA)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, executing, and assessing Department of Defense public affairs (PA) and visual information (VI) support during domestic support to civil authorities (DSCA) and other domestic operations, including JIC, communications strategy, annex development, media engagement, and release procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment requirements for PA and VI personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: When required, PA and VI personnel, who deploy in support of domestic operations, should have a cellular phone and a laptop computer with wireless access or an aircard. PA personnel with access to portable broadcast quality imagery transmission systems should be prepared to deploy with and support operations with those systems. PA and VI personnel should deploy with digital cameras and have still and motion imagery editing and data transfer software on their laptops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Personnel will not always have access to the '.mil' domain during domestic operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement: NRF knowledge and FEMA courses
rubrics_metrics.description: All PA and VI personnel ordered to deploy in support of domestic operations should have working knowledge of the NRF as it pertains to PA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online Federal Emergency Management Agency training courses are available at http://training.fema.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA planning objective (ESF #15 support)
rubrics_metrics.description: PA plans for DSCA are tailored to support the ESF #15 requirement to provide accurate, coordinated, timely, and accessible information to affected audiences, including governments, media, the private sector, and the local populace, including the special needs population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA activities must be planned, coordinated, and integrated across jurisdictions, agencies, and organizations both government and private.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans must delineate responsibilities, processes, and logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planners ensure that plans and associated annexes delineate responsibilities, processes, and logistics as appropriate in support of ESF #15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annexes should explicitly assign roles and logistical support to avoid gaps during execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate messages with federal, state, tribal, and local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination of messages with federal, state, tribal, and local governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure message alignment across jurisdictions to prevent conflicting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for the MOC
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide support for the Mission/Media Operations Center (MOC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include staffing, connectivity, and procedures to interface with the MOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering incident information
rubrics_metrics.description: Gathering information on the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish processes to collect timely, accurate incident data to inform public releases and media engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide incident information and imagery in accessible formats/multiple languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing incident-related information and imagery through the media and other sources in accessible formats and multiple languages (as necessary) to individuals, households, businesses, and industries directly or indirectly affected by the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for accessible (e.g., alt text, captioning) and translated products to reach special needs and non-English-speaking populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor news coverage to ensure accurate information dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring news coverage to ensure that accurate information is disseminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use media monitoring to detect inaccuracies and correct misinformation promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle special PA projects (press ops, news conferences, dignitary tours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling appropriate special projects such as news conferences and press operations for incident area tours by government officials and other dignitaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate leads, timelines, and security coordination for special events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide basic services to assist the news media
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing basic services, such as communications and supplies, to assist the news media in disseminating information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include media support (e.g., filing capability, workspaces) in logistics planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise participation and capability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: PA and VI personnel participate in exercises and conduct objective assessments of capabilities so that issues are identified and remedied prior to a real incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises should validate procedures, staffing, equipment, and interagency coordination; results should feed planning updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise planning: integrate interagency PA working groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise planning provides an exceptional opportunity to inform other agencies about DOD PA roles, responsibilities, and capabilities. Interagency PA working groups should be integrated into the joint exercise lifecycle process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for both 'real-world' and 'simulated media' requirements during exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise execution: practice real-world dissemination and interagency coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: During exercises, DOD PA and VI participants have the opportunity to perform PA operations in the exercise’s scenario being simulated, participate in dissemination of real-world information to exercise participants, and practice with other agencies during events that can draw significant media and public attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exercises to rehearse media engagement, JIC procedures, and info-release workflows under stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution phase: Shaping (manage expectations and develop themes/messages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaping: PA manages expectations regarding DOD’s response among both the public and the other responding agencies. PA activities include developing themes and messages that clearly explain the scope and timing of the DOD response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively set realistic expectations to reduce confusion about DOD role and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution phase: Engagement (active information dissemination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement: This is the phase where military forces are actually on-scene supporting an incident and PA is actively informing the public about DOD activities via releases of information and imagery, press conferences, and site visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate content and cadence of releases with JIC/primary agency to maintain consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution phase: Transition (explain disengagement of DOD support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition: This is the phase where military forces begin to disengage from incident response support. It is critical that PA activities in this phase articulate why DOD support is no longer required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear messaging about transfer of responsibilities and continued actions by civilian agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial DOD PA involvement via DCO/DCE and liaison roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial DOD PA involvement in DSCA will be through the defense coordinating officer (DCO) assigned to the applicable DHS/FEMA region and the defense coordinating element (DCE) if established. PA personnel provide initial assessments of situation to the DCO, DCE, and combatant command PA staff in terms of requirements for personnel and equipment. They provide initial interface with other deployed federal public information officers (PIOs), and serve as the DOD liaison for the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure early PA liaison presence to shape coordination and establish information flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed PA element in unit headquarters for media engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Other units tasked to deploy in support of domestic operations should also include a PA element in their headquarters staff. This PA element should be prepared to actively engage the media to show how the unit is supporting the federal response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign PA staff with clear authorities and access to command information to support timely engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information Center (JIC) establishment and location
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC is normally located close to the best sources of information about the situation, such as an incident command post or emergency operations center. A single JIC location is preferable, but the system is flexible and adaptable enough to accommodate virtual or multiple JIC locations, as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate JICs to maximize access to incident data and to facilitate interagency coordination; plan for virtual connectivity if physical co-location not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC staffing and assignment responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When a JIC is established, the responsible commander ensures that adequate PA personnel are assigned whenever DOD forces deploy. However, the bulk of DOD PA personnel supporting the incident will be assigned to the JFC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan personnel assignments to balance JIC needs and unit-level media support.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC primary responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC carries out the PIO’s responsibilities and has three primary responsibilities: (a) Gather incident data. (b) Analyze public perceptions of the response. (c) Inform the public and serve as the source of accurate and comprehensive information about the incident and the response to a specific set of audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize JIC functions (news desk, media relations, analysis) to ensure timely collection, assessment, and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate DOD PA releases with primary agency/JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD PA releases its own information and imagery, and conducts media operations, but the products should be coordinated with either the primary agency or the JIC to ensure consistent messages and avoid the release of conflicting or incident-sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clearance/coordination workflows and message approval authorities to prevent conflicting releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and use the National Incident Communications Conference Line (NICCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: During DSCA, combatant command PA personnel monitor the NICCL that is used for transmission and exchange of critical and timely (e.g., 'breaking') incident information among federal and affected state, local, and tribal authorities. It is a key source of emerging information for PA activities and communications synchronization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and distribute NICCL summaries; DHS PA may continuously monitor NICCL for critical incidents; use NICCL for daily coordination calls during sustained incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop DOD Public Affairs Guidance (PAG)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OASD(PA) will develop PAG for domestic operations that is consistent with that of other operations and DHS PAG, but also includes relevant information from non-DOD participants. Additionally, while DOD PAG does not apply to other agencies, it should be coordinated with and distributed to all participating organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PAG is not appropriate or feasible, the PAO may produce a PA strategy document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing assessment of public communications
rubrics_metrics.description: On-going assessment of public communication activities by DOD PA personnel is critical to support follow-on planning as well as inform future operations. PAOs and PA staffs conduct analysis of international coverage of DOD activities to assess the character of their reporting as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessments to refine messaging, identify perception trends, and adjust operational communications strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications strategy must align with strategic communication themes
rubrics_metrics.description: The commander’s communications strategy should be an element of the commander’s larger overall strategy and is supported by the broader SC effort. Commanders who develop and execute communication strategies derived from and aligned with SC themes and messages increase the opportunity for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make communications strategy commander-driven, proactive, and consider effects on the information environment prior to execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate communications strategy with other instruments of national power
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications strategy facilititates coordinated communication efforts focused on reaching individual audiences via the most credible and effective means available. Commanders should be cognizant of the impact that joint force communications activities have on the other three instruments of national power (diplomatic, informational, and economic) as well as their implications for the total operational environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate messaging with OGAs, multinational partners, and NGOs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use planning guidance sources to shape communications strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial planning guidance sources used to develop the communications strategy include the overall USG strategy and SC guidance, SecDef and Joint Chiefs of Staff guidance as well as the associated combatant command regional strategy and the joint force mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the joint force use theater campaign plan, operation plan, commander’s planning guidance, and desired outcomes to shape communications across current and future operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-functional working group for strategy development
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications strategy development is often accomplished in a cross-functional working group. Input from key functional staff members informed by information from various levels above and below the joint force headquarters as well as assessment of past activities helps communication planners refine future efforts and messages to better meet stated communication objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PA, IO, POLAD, SJA, CMO, embassies, host nation, and other stakeholders in coordination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA role in strategy execution and responsibility of all personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: PA plays a large role in the execution of the communications strategy through the dissemination of information and other traditional communication products to various audiences. Supporting the execution of the communications strategy requires the attention of everyone in the joint force, from the commander to the individual servicemember whose actions as well as words can be exploited by the adversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train all personnel on information environment risks and messaging discipline consistent with OPSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex development: Situation must identify responsibilities and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigns responsibilities and guidance for military PA actions (public information, command and internal information, and community engagement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify enemy expectations, friendly agencies contributing to PA effort, and host-nation preferences/sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex development: State mission as essential PA tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: State clearly and concisely the essential PA tasks to be accomplished as they relate to the overall operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mission statements should tie PA tasks directly to the commander’s intent and operation objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex execution: Concept of operations and specific PA tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline PA efforts for the operation as part of JFC’s mission and concept of the operation. Outline the PA tasks to be completed during the listed phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks should include release authority guidance, casualty/mortuary affairs, POW/MIA/EPW matters, MOC consideration, and COMCAM/VI requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex logistics: detailed personnel and equipment support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed personnel and equipment support requirements to component commands. Address access to the on-scene commander (OSC), supported CCDR, and the DOS representative, and to the secure voice circuit that connects the MOC; access to hard copy message facilities; intertheater and intratheater transportation for escorted media; access to secure and nonsecure Internet that connects the MOC to other PA outlets; access to digital imagery receiver equipment; access to equipment for review and release of battle damage assessment-type video footage (could be through COMCAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate this annex with logistics, communications, IO, and other planners to ensure required support is detailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinating instructions: release, IO support, interviews, records
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify procedures for coordination of release of information, PA support to IO, coordination of requests for interviews and news conferences with unit and Service PA offices and staff judge advocate for EPW or detained personnel, outline required PA coordination with other staff elements involved in release of information outside the command, and establish procedures for keeping PA historical records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document clearance processes, legal coordination steps, and records retention requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media ground rules: release of cleared information and category guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish means for release of information to be cleared and made available to the press. Provide precise guidance for release of specific categories of information to the media, and provide guidance on specific categories of information not releasable to the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define processes and authorities for classifying information as releasable or not releasable in the annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration & logistics: OPSEC and AV/VI coverage procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify administration and logistics requirements for PA support. Identify OPSEC procedures for PA personnel, include security review procedures. Identify procedures for providing PA, audio-visual, and VI coverage of the operation, including COMCAM requirements. Identify internal information requirements for subordinate and component commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure security review and OPSEC vetting are embedded in AV/VI product workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC/Sub-MOC support: personnel, equipment, services
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify required personnel; identify additional standard equipment required to allow MOC or sub-MOC operation in the operational area (include tentage and individual field equipment on the same basis of issue as the accompanied unit); include basic food and shelter, water, office space and materials, clothing, transportation, portable copying machines, communications, automated data processing support, Internet and WWW access, and facsimile machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to sustain MOC operations for the expected duration and coordinate resupply contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media/media pool support: comprehensive media support planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify details on supporting the media to include: facilities, messing, billeting, force protection, immunizations, emergency medical treatment, transportation and communications, access to unclassified operational information, media pools, and other support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contingency plans for media safety and movement in contested or hazardous areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media pool operational specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline plans for support of the media pool including daily, comprehensive, unclassified operational briefings; access to areas of ongoing operations; access to key command and staff personnel; designated officer from the supported command assigned to coordinate media pool requirements; itinerary planning to enable media pool to disperse throughout the combat area and to regroup periodically to share information and file stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate liaison officers and schedule regular briefings to maintain pool functionality and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required logistic support for media pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline supported commander responsibilities for planning logistics support for pool and escort personnel addressing: existing airlift to/from the point of origin and the operational area; theater ground, sea, and air transportation available to the media; messing, billeting, and reimbursement requirements; issuance of any equipment considered appropriate to the situation (e.g., helmets, canteens, protective vest, and chemical protective gear); access to communications facilities to file stories on an expedited basis; medical support; religious support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify responsibilities for cost, reimbursement, and issuance of protective gear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release authority and public statements procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Until release authority is delegated to them, units should forward queries and proposed news releases to the combatant command PAO. No public statements concerning operations should be made by subordinate units without prior coordination with the combatant command PAO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish delegation criteria and document authorized release levels in PAG or annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions about media behavior and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumptions: (1) All statements will be 'on the record.' (2) News media will have the ability to transmit instantaneous live reports from the operational area. (3) News media coverage will be highly competitive, with a tendency to seek access to the operational area and report events as they happen. (4) News media already on the scene may find ways to get to the operational area(s) and report the activities as they happen without regard for security concerns. (5) Independent media may be simultaneously deployed with the DOD Media Pool at the invitation of the Service component headquarters, under guidelines established by combatant command PAO that differ from those which apply to the DOD Media Pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for rapid, on-the-record communications and anticipate uncontrolled media access; include independent media considerations in PAG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security instructions for PA products and briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs submitting or staffing proposed products for public release must ensure that the information contained therein is fully coordinated and properly classified until approved for release. Media are not usually given access to classified information that could jeopardize operations or endanger lives. In circumstances where this may be appropriate, PAOs must gain specific approval from the JFC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'security at the source' principle: individuals meeting with journalists are responsible for ensuring no classified or sensitive info is revealed; photographers should be directed not to take pictures of classified areas or equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for briefing media with withheld-release agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some members of the media may be briefed on planned operations prior to execution if they agree to withhold release until permitted to do so by the appropriate military authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document conditions for embargoed briefings and secure concurrence from appropriate authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release below JFC level procedures and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon delegation of release authority, component and subordinate commanders may release information within the bounds of policy and guidance set forth by the joint force PAO or MOC director. A verbatim record of releases and news conferences should be maintained. Subordinate commanders should report the substance of any interview or responses to query to the MOC. News conferences should be videotaped or audiotaped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain auditable records of public statements and reporters' interactions for accountability and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA and Privacy Act coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for information under the Freedom of Information Act Program should be coordinated through the command’s designated Freedom of Information Act representative or the servicing staff judge advocate or legal advisor if no such representative exists. DOD personnel shall not disclose any personal information contained in any system of records except as authorized by DOD 5400.11-R, DOD Privacy Program, or other applicable law or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate legal review for FOIA/Privacy Act releases; willful prohibited disclosures may result in penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for media discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation results in more effective discussions with the media. Central to the process is identifying what information is to be released based on prevailing PAG and OPSEC. Commanders, briefers, and PA personnel should be aware of the basic facts of any operation and sensitive to the various consequences of communicating them to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use key message templates and anticipate difficult questions; vet talking points through OPSEC/legal channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA assessment: categories usually releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: The following categories of information are usually releasable, though individual situations may require modifications: (1) The arrival of US units in the operational area once officially announced; (2) Approximate friendly force strength and equipment figures; (3) Approximate friendly casualty and POW figures by Service; (4) Nonsensitive, unclassified information regarding US air, land, sea, space, and special operations, past and present; (5) In general terms, identification and location of military targets and objectives previously attacked and the types of ordnance expended; (6) Date, time, or location of previous military missions and actions as well as mission results; (7) Number of combat air patrol or reconnaissance missions and/or sorties flown; (8) Weather and climate conditions; (9) If appropriate, allied participation by type; (10) Conventional operations’ unclassified code names; (11) Names of installations and assigned units; (12) Size of friendly force participating in an action or operation using general terms such as 'multi-battalion,' or 'naval task force;' (13) Types of forces involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When releasing information, use general terms rather than specific numeric or tactical details unless cleared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified/sensitive information categories not to reveal
rubrics_metrics.description: Classified aspects of equipment, procedures, and operations must be protected. The following categories should not be revealed: (1) Specific numerical information on troop strength, aircraft, weapons systems, or supplies; (2) Any information that reveals details of future plans, operations, or strikes; (3) Information and imagery that would reveal the specific location of military forces or show the level of security at military installations or encampments; (4) Rules of engagement; (5) Information on intelligence activities, including sources and methods; (6) Specific information on troop movement or size, tactical deployments and dispositions during operations; (7) Identification of mission aircraft points of origin (other than land- or carrier-based); (8) Information on the effectiveness or ineffectiveness of weapon systems and tactics; (9) Specific identifying information on missing or downed personnel while search and rescue operations are planned or underway; (10) SOF methods, equipment, or tactics which, if disclosed, would cause serious harm to the ability of these forces to accomplish their mission; (11) Information on operational or support vulnerabilities that could be used against US or allied units until that information no longer provides tactical advantage; (12) Specific operating methods and tactics (use general terms); (13) Requests for interviews or filming of EPWs or detained personnel must be coordinated through the staff judge advocate and generally are likely to be prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt this list to the operational context and ensure legal/SJA clearance where required.
